old: The system has five principal responsibilities. React owns interface composition and subscribes to a controller snapshot. GameController owns the game-facing action boundary, current-player choice, AI-turn lifecycle and notification. The core owns board cells, legal-move history and rule evaluation. Pixi owns the visual board and converts gestures through an input/coordinate layer. The AI adapter owns search dispatch and Worker resources; it proposes a move but does not directly mutate the authoritative application board [4], [2], [5], [18].

old: MatchController defines setup, ready, playing and game-over. Its initial state is ready, local two-player mode, normal difficulty and round identifier zero. Calling playCell from setup or ready invokes startRound, which increments the round identifier, clears the old outcome and enters playing. An accepted win or full-board draw changes the match to game-over. The thinking flag belongs to the AI request lifecycle; it is not a fifth value in the phase enumeration [33], [2].

old: The ordered search visits only 2,164 nodes, but performs 48,841 extra ordering evaluations and has a median of 68,457 µs. The counterexample is important: fewer recursively visited nodes do not necessarily mean lower elapsed time, because ranking candidates also costs work. At depth one, ordering cannot prune a lower level and can add overhead. The run uses native std::time::Instant, excludes state cloning and table/Zobrist initialization from the timer, has only three sequential controlled repeats, and does not randomize order or pin a CPU. Values must not be presented as browser timings [49].

Separate adapter and browser records exercise the connection between search and the application. old: The active search is selective. Its soft tactical cap retains immediate winning and blocking completions, but deeper positional moves remain subject to the candidate limit. The configured limit falls from 15 at Hard to 8 at Master as depth rises from two to five plies. The static evaluator scores contiguous runs; gapped formations and intersecting threats depend on tactical assessment and deeper search. Persistent transposition tables and iterative-deepening budgets are studied in separate implementations rather than used by the active Rust search [10], [29], [13].
